newsitem.title: USA: U.S. official meets Kurdish factions.
newsitem.headline: U.S. official meets Kurdish factions.

text.p: A senior U.S. official met on Thursday with representatives of the two rival Kurdish factions in northern Iraq in a fresh bid to limit the influence of Iraqi President Saddam Hussein in the area.

Assistant Secretary of State Robert Pelletreau met delegations of the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) and Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK), the State Department said. British and Turkish officials also attended.

A KDP decision last August to invite Iraqi troops into the Western-protected Kurdish region to help oust the PUK from the city of Arbil sparked two months of fighting between the two factions, ended by a U.S.-brokered ceasefire.

The increased influence this gave Baghdad in the region forced an end to the Western military presence there. The United States also evacuated more than 6,000 Kurds and Iraqis it feared could be in danger from Saddam.
"These are preliminary negotiations to try to make sure that we can contribute to stability in northern Iraq," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said of Thursday's talks.

"We're talking here about the efforts to consolidate the ceasefire ... make sure that Saddam's influence is severely limited and promote some kind of a reconciliation between these two Kurdish groups," he added.
Burns said it remained to be seen whether further talks would be held bringing in KDP leader Massoud Barzani and PUK leader Jalal Talabani, neither of whom attended Thursday's meeting.
Although no major fighting has occurred since October, the two groups remain divided over oil trade revenues on the Turkish border and the status of Arbil.
